title: DM Rush: Influencer Edition
premise: A fast arcade-style moderation game where the player manages an influencer's live feed by reacting correctly to descending fan and hater messages.
interaction_model: Single-screen binary input game; tap or click the left half of the screen to LOVE supportive messages and the right half to BLOCK hostile messages, always affecting the lowest active message bubble.
objective: Earn the highest possible Verified Fans score by correctly classifying incoming chat bubbles while preventing the life meter from dropping to zero.
progression: Endless run structure with continuously increasing difficulty: correct responses raise score and slightly increase speed/spawn pressure, while mistakes and missed bubbles drain life until game over.
theme: Neon influencer-stream satire with social media chat moderation framing.
mood: Punchy, reactive, playful, slightly chaotic, and arcade-tense.
likely_audience: players who enjoy quick reflex classification games
confidence_notes: High confidence in the left/right classification loop, score/life model, and endless escalation because these are explicit in code.
High confidence that the fiction is influencer/chat moderation themed because of the title, HUD labels, message text, and game-over copy.
Moderate confidence in taxonomy labels such as lane runner versus clicker/reaction game, since the game borrows traits from several casual arcade categories without literal running.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly single-screen arcade game called "DM Rush: Influencer Edition" where the player moderates an influencer's incoming live-feed messages in real time. Present the game in a neon cyberpop social-media style with a full-screen canvas, glossy glass HUD panels, bold futuristic display text, and a dark purple-to-indigo gradient background with subtle grid and glow effects. The core loop is an endless score chase: rounded chat bubbles descend from the top toward the bottom, each representing either a supportive fan message or a hostile hater message. The player does not tap bubbles directly; instead, tapping or clicking the left half of the screen performs LOVE and tapping or clicking the right half performs BLOCK, always applying the action to the lowest currently active bubble as the most urgent target. Fan bubbles should be pink/red with heart-like iconography and short positive text such as "First like!" or "You're trending!" while hater bubbles should be green with warning/toxic iconography and short negative text such as "Spam alert" or "Hard pass." A correct response removes the bubble, awards points shown as Verified Fans, triggers positive sound/visual feedback, emits emoji particles, and slightly increases difficulty. A wrong response or a missed bubble costs life from a percentage-based meter, triggers failure feedback, screen shake, and a harsher reaction cue. Difficulty should ramp up continuously through faster effective movement and more frequent spawns rather than discrete levels. Include quick audiovisual juice such as looping background music, score and fail sound effects, GIF-like reaction popups, vibration support when available, and a dramatic game-over overlay that says the feed has shut down because too many bad messages slipped through. Show a final fan count and allow an immediate restart into a fresh endless run. Preserve the playful influencer satire tone, the binary left-versus-right decision pattern, the urgency of acting on the lowest bubble, and the overall feel of a fast casual mobile reflex game.
